medications.purpose: Lifelong secondary prevention of cardiovascular events in IHD
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends low‑dose aspirin for all patients with confirmed IHD (first‑line antiplatelet).

medications.purpose: Reduce non‑HDL cholesterol by >40% and lower risk of recurrent events
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends a high‑intensity statin for every patient with IHD (first‑line).

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily, titrate to 10 mg as tolerated
medications.purpose: First‑line anti‑anginal therapy; target resting HR 55‑60 bpm
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 lists beta‑blockers as first‑line anti‑anginal agents for IHD.

medications.purpose: Cardioprotective ACE‑I for hypertension, diabetes and IHD (already prescribed)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends ACE‑inhibitors for all IHD patients, especially with hypertension/diabetes.

medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive and second‑line anti‑anginal (already prescribed)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 lists CCBs as second‑line anti‑anginal if beta‑blocker insufficient.
NICE CG126 recommends BP control as part of IHD management.

medications.purpose: Gastro‑protection due to aspirin use and low platelet count
medications.nice_justification: NICE advises PPI co‑prescription for patients at high GI bleed risk on aspirin.

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased risk of bleeding due to thrombocytopenia
interactions_checked.action: Check full blood count; consider delaying aspirin if platelets <100×10⁹/L, use PPI, monitor for bleeding.

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Monitor CK if muscle symptoms; consider dose reduction of atorvastatin if CK rises.

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering and risk of hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start bisoprolol at low dose, titrate slowly; monitor BP and symptoms at each dialysis session.

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined antihypertensive effect may cause hypotension or bradycardia
interactions_checked.action: Monitor heart rate and BP; adjust doses if HR <55 bpm or symptomatic hypotension.

interactions_checked.interaction: Thiazides raise serum uric acid, potentially worsening gout
interactions_checked.action: Monitor uric acid; consider switching to a potassium‑sparing diuretic if gout flares increase.
Educate patient on glucose monitoring; review insulin doses given low glucose readings.

contraindications.reason: Patient has end‑stage renal disease; NSAIDs increase cardiovascular and renal risk (NICE contraindicated).
Contraindicated with beta‑blocker due to risk of heart block (NICE).

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided; assumed ESRD on dialysis – ACE‑I dose kept but renal function and potassium will be monitored per NICE.
Platelet MPV critically low – aspirin risk flagged; decision to start aspirin should be revisited after CBC.
Blood pressure values unavailable – titration of antihypertensives will be guided by in‑clinic readings.
HbA1c 2.9% is unusually low – possible lab error or hypoglycaemia; insulin regimen requires urgent review.
Allergy status not documented – verify no hypersensitivity to aspirin, statin or beta‑blocker before initiation.
treatment_summary: Start low‑dose aspirin with PPI gastro‑protection, high‑intensity atorvastatin, and low‑dose bisoprolol for secondary prevention and angina control, while continuing lisinopril, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide. Monitor renal function, potassium, blood pressure, heart rate, platelet count, CK and glucose closely, especially given dialysis, low platelet volume and risk of hypoglycaemia. Adjust doses as needed and avoid NSAIDs and verapamil per NICE CG126/NG185.
